_note: Every on-demand practice's applies_to, with the reason, as reviewable data.
EVERY on-demand practice is listed, including the ones deliberately left at
'**' -- a decision to leave a practice unrouted has to be visible, not an
omission. This is the same discipline tools/section_split.json uses for the
'**' means the path channel never fires for this practice: it is reachable

GATES are the fourth loading channel: a named MOMENT, not a place. A practice whose occasion is a moment cannot be reached by a glob, however well written -- that is why 26 entries here stay at '**'. tools/precedent_gate.py loads a gate's practices at the moment it is reached.
through the occasion index, a gate, or a check, and the 'why' says which.
tools/verify_harness.py fails if practices/*.md and this file disagree.

THE RULE THIS PASS SETTLED ON, after two rounds of narrowing: a glob is justified only where the path identifies the practice's DISTINGUISHING condition, not merely a necessary one. 'A rule is being written' is necessary for volatile-rules-carry-dates and not distinguishing; 'a new rule is being written' IS distinguishing for cite-the-incident. Applying that uniformly is what stopped this pass from becoming a search for globs that make a number move.

acronyms-glossary.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

affordance-is-shared.why: No locus. 'A mechanism that makes something reachable' is a property of what you built, not of where you built it.

bold-key-phrases.why: Its own applies_to. The occasion is writing any document meant to be read, so the path channel fires on markdown and nothing else -- and it is tier: resident anyway, so the path glob is a second reminder rather than the only one.

build-buy-decompose.why: A decision, made before any file exists.

capture-gate.why: A moment, not a place — routed by the `merge` gate instead.

catalogue-carries-stories.why: Set from the Install text, which names practices/*.md unambiguously: the check reads every practice file's frontmatter status and its ## Story. Deliberately not '**' -- nothing outside practices/ can violate it.

check-source-architecture.why: A reasoning step about options, with no artifact.

checkable-gets-checked.why: Fires when a new practice is written, same locus as cite-the-incident, whose glob this copies directly.
checkable-gets-checked.gates_why: Whether a check was genuinely attempted is a judgment a review makes, the same as mistakes-become-rules' proportionality guard.

cite-the-incident.why: A new convention or rule is written into the catalogue. That is a place, not just a moment, and its check already scopes there.
cite-the-incident.gates_why: A review that produces a rule produces it here; it also has a glob for where the rule is written.

code-cites-practice.why: The occasion is writing code because a practice requires it, which happens in tools/ -- this repo's only place code implementing a practice's behavior is written.

computed-numbers-in-scripts.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

control-asserts-which-failure.why: Its own applies_to. A control lives with the code it controls, and in this repo that is tools/ -- verify_harness.py and the check scripts are where every planted case is written. The test-file globs carry it to repos laid out conventionally, which this one is not. Deliberately not '**': the occasion is writing a test, and a glob over everything would surface it on documents and practice files where there is no control to assert anything about.
control-asserts-which-failure.gates_why: Asking 'what else could produce this failure?' is a reviewer's question about a diff that adds a control, the same shape as checkable-gets-checked's review gate.

convention-to-audit.why: A moment — routed by the `review` gate instead.
convention-to-audit.gates_why: Fires when a convention is violated, which is something a review notices.

cross-source-rollout.why: A moment, not a place -- what makes a change cross-source-relevant is its meaning, not which file it touched, so no glob identifies it. Routed by the `merge` gate instead.
cross-source-rollout.decided: 2026-09-05, same session that added very-deep-check's source-presence and stale-branch additions
cross-source-rollout.gates_why: The rollout (or the blocked-on TODO standing in for it) has to happen before the thread ends, the same timing capture-gate and todo-is-a-handoff already use.

deliverables-look-like-output.why: A reader-facing deliverable is a document. Its check already runs over changed markdown; the glob makes the Rule reachable at the same scope.

disclose-landing.why: A moment — routed by the `reply` gate instead.
disclose-landing.gates_why: Its occasion is the reply that follows a landing or a candidate being raised.

doc-references-are-links.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

docs-are-current-state.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

docs-track-models.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

document-status-header.why: Its own applies_to, and the path IS the distinguishing condition: the standard is scoped to those two trees by definition, so a glob over them is exactly the practice's own scope rather than an approximation of it. Deliberately not '**/*.md' -- a document at the repository root or in documentation/ is out of scope, and surfacing the Rule there would be telling a reader to stamp a file the check will never look at.

engine-plus-host-shims.why: The occasion is EXPORTING a tool across a repo boundary, which happens in the vendored tree and the host shims -- not in tools/, where the engine is merely authored. A first draft of this pass used tools/** and surfaced the practice on 10 of 20 eval cases against 3 it applies to; re-reading the occasion is what narrowed it, not the cost figure, though the cost figure is what prompted the re-read.

fail-gracefully.why: DELIBERATELY UNROUTED, and the reason is the practice's own scope. It governs code that depends on anything outside its own control -- any language, any file, plus setup and configuration that is not code at all. No glob narrower than ** would be honest: restricting it to tools/**/*.py would silence it for shell hooks, templates and workflow files, which are exactly where the container's defaults bite. Its own Install already records that the general form floods a mechanical check (67 hits against this repo's tools/, mostly legitimate), so the occasion index and review carry it rather than the path channel.

frame-from-audience-question.why: No path tells you who the audience is.

full-practice-audit.why: Not a place -- a whole-catalogue sweep is invoked explicitly by a person, not triggered by touching any one file. Reachability comes from its occasion clause.

generated-artifact-provenance.why: Where this repo actually builds and commits generated artifacts. Narrow on purpose: a glob over everything a build might touch would fire constantly and say nothing.

github-setup-disclosed.why: The distinguishing condition is that the install step is GitHub-SPECIFIC, and the workflow files are exactly that. INSTALL.md and SETUP.md were in a first draft of this glob; they are where the fact must be DISCLOSED, not what makes the practice fire, and including them surfaced it on half the eval cases.

heading-outline.why: Wide on purpose, and the counterpart to headline-capitalization's narrow glob. Whether an outline is BROKEN is not a matter of audience -- a skipped level misfiles a section in any renderer, in a spec or a practice file exactly as in a published page -- while how a heading is STYLED only matters where people outside the project read it. The two halves came out of one retired team rule that bound both to `**/*.md`; splitting the scopes is the point of splitting the slugs. Measured before it was set: the whole tracked tree had exactly one violation, in generated output, so the wide glob costs no backlog.

headline-capitalization.why: `**` because the scope is an EXCLUSION, and a glob cannot express one. Every document is outward-facing unless tools/title_case.py names it internal (INTERNAL_DIRS/INTERNAL_FILES), which is the one definition both the gate and this practice read. Written as an allowlist it decayed within a day -- the practice shipped covering `documentation/` alone and `content/` and `book*/` had to be added the same afternoon, so an unclassified new directory would have been missed silently. This way the path-trigger fires a little wider than the gate enforces, which is the harmless direction: the reader is reminded on a practice file and the check then says it is out of scope. Morgan settled the boundary 2026-09-06: capitalization is for what outsiders read, and internal working files are never to be 'fixed'.

index-remembers-past.why: Fires on the relationship between two documents, which a path cannot see.

label-describes-content.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

layered-practice-packs.why: Deciding where a new rule belongs happens where rules and the source declaration live.

lead-with-what-it-is.why: Phase 1 scoped this to README.md alone from the Install text, but the practice's own occasion is "writing a README or other project-facing entry document" -- and AGENTS.md's own Conventions section (readers-vocabulary) already names SETUP.md and templates/GETTING_STARTED.md alongside README.md as this repo's other outward-facing entry documents. Left at README.md only, the glob silently missed the two files the occasion's own "or other" clause names.
lead-with-what-it-is.decided: phase 1, widened in the 2026-09-02 deep-check pass

merge-authorization-keyword.why: RETIRED 2026-09-07 -- kept here because the routing check still reads every on-demand practice file, and an entry that vanishes reads as one nobody decided. It routes nothing: a retired practice is not in force. Was: a moment, routed by the `merge` gate instead.
merge-authorization-keyword.gates_why: Fires when the standing merge instruction is used.

merge-runbook.why: A moment — routed by the `merge` gate instead.
merge-runbook.gates_why: Fires when merging a branch that touches shared files.

migration-scrubs-vocabulary.why: A moment (migrating off an old system) rather than a place -- reachable only through the occasion index, since no gate exists for a moment this rare.

mistakes-become-rules.why: A moment — routed by the `review` gate instead. Its proportionality guard is also why it has no check.
mistakes-become-rules.gates_why: Its occasion is 'a review finds a defect'. No path reaches a moment.

name-both-sides-of-ledger.why: Domain-specific to work this repo does not do; no locus here.

no-rewrite-for-warnings.why: A moment — routed by the `push` gate, and enforced by a turn-end check.
no-rewrite-for-warnings.gates_why: The moment a tool complains about published history is the moment before a push.

no-version-suffix.why: Applies to any added file, which is what `**` means. Its check covers it at exactly that scope.

one-formatter-per-quantity.why: Fires on how a quantity is printed, not on which file prints it.

open-item-disposition.why: The item's disposition is written in the TODO file itself, and the template teaches the convention to every dependent repo. Nowhere else can carry one.
open-item-disposition.gates_why: Half the rule fires at a moment no path reaches -- a session writing its reply, deciding whether to raise an item at all.

outward-summary-discipline.why: No path identifies an outward-facing summary.

parallel-artifact-ledger.why: templates/harness/{claude-code,codex,gemini-cli} is a literal parallel family: a change to one raises the transfer question for the others.

permutation-frontier-column.why: Fires on the shape of a table being built, not its location.

pr-template-honest-gates.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

practice-export-loop.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.
practice-export-loop.gates_why: The export gate fires before a thread ends; a merge is where that is checked.

quote-discipline.why: Fires on whose figure you are quoting, which a path cannot see.

readers-vocabulary.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

registry-source-of-truth.why: Genuinely unroutable — see spec/LOADER.md. A registry is recognised by what it is for, and this repo's are .json, .py and .md alike.

rename-updates-links.why: A rename can strand a reference in any file of any type -- a markdown link, a path inside a script, a workflow, a config -- so no narrower glob is honest. `**` is right here for the same reason it is right for no-version-suffix: the occasion is an action taken ON a file, not a property of the file being edited. Its check is scoped instead: it compares against the published default branch, so it only ever asks about renames this branch itself made.

reply-links-files.gates_why: Its occasion is the reply itself.
reply-links-files.why: Resident; its applies_to is not this file's business.

repo-is-memory.gates_why: A turn ending is when knowledge either got committed or was lost.
repo-is-memory.why: Resident; its applies_to is not this file's business.

decommission-deletes-files.why: No locus, and `**` for the same reason rename-updates-links and no-version-suffix take it: the occasion is an action taken ON a path -- retiring the mechanism that owned it -- not a property of the file being edited. A retirement can land in any file type, and the file most in need of deleting is usually one nobody is editing at all, so a narrower glob would fire least where it matters most. Its check is scoped instead, to the paths this repo has declared retired.

routing-audit.why: Not a place -- "checking whether practices that should have fired, fired" is a periodic act a person invokes, not a file-touch trigger. Reachability comes from its occasion clause.

scripts-assert-properties.why: No path locus, and a glob would contradict the practice's own scope gate: 'Scripts that own their own numbers end to end need nothing. Keep the instrumented list explicit.' That explicit list IS the routing mechanism, and it exists -- model_audit's INSTRUMENTED. A glob over tools/** would surface the Rule on every script and is exactly the over-instrumentation the gate forbids.

scrub-gate.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.
scrub-gate.gates_why: The public tree must be clean at merge and at push, which are the two moments it can be checked.

search-by-purpose.why: Fires at the start of work, before any file is touched. Its check enforces the findable-output half only.

second-pass-capture.why: A moment — routed by the `merge` gate instead.
second-pass-capture.gates_why: Its occasion says 'before the merge-time capture gate' in so many words.

section-order-by-frequency.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

session-bootstrap.why: Session setup lives in hooks and bootstrap scripts. The tightest locus in this pass.

source-naming.why: Declaring a source IS editing precedent.json, so the path identifies the practice's distinguishing condition rather than merely a necessary one. The Rule's other half -- say the convention before anyone picks a name -- is a conversational moment with no file at all, and no gate reaches it either; the occasion index carries that half, which is why the occasion names importing and creating a repository, not only declaring one.
source-naming.decided: 2026-09-06, the session that landed the practice

tabular-shared-renderer.why: Fires on publishing a table, which no path in this repo identifies.

todo-is-a-handoff.why: The distinguishing condition is writing or triaging an entry in the TODO file itself — the only place the practice's rule is ever violated.
todo-is-a-handoff.gates_why: The periodic sweep that enforces the stated-reason requirement on the backlog naturally happens at merge time, the same as capture-gate.

two-check-levels.why: Fires once, when a repo names its check levels. Nothing recurring to trigger on.

variant-re-derives.why: Fires on the relationship between a thing and its variant.

verify-decomposition.why: Fires on a computed total being reported, wherever that happens.

verify-postcondition.gates_why: The postconditions it names are git state, checked before a push and at the end of a turn.
verify-postcondition.why: Resident; its applies_to is not this file's business.

very-deep-check.why: Not a place -- a whole-repo coherence review is invoked explicitly by a person, or after drift-inviting work, not triggered by touching any one file. Reachability comes from its occasion clause, the same as its full-practice-audit and routing-audit siblings.
very-deep-check.decided: 2026-09-05, TODO.md item 17 session (RPP 'very deep check' enumerated and wired)

volatile-rules-carry-dates.why: The path identifies 'a rule is being written', which is necessary but not distinguishing -- the practice fires only when the rule depends on the OUTSIDE WORLD, and no path can see that. A glob on the rule locus surfaced it on 13 of 20 eval cases against 4 it applies to.

write-like-a-human.why: Its own applies_to. The occasion is writing anything a person will read, so the path channel fires on markdown and nothing else -- and it is tier: resident anyway, so the glob is a second reminder rather than the only channel. The half no glob can reach is the chat reply, which is why it also carries the `reply` gate.

durable-fix.why: A moment, not a file class — it fires while deciding WHERE a fix goes, which is before any particular file is chosen, and applies to every kind of fix (code, document, config, container state). Routed by the `review` and `reply` gates instead.
durable-fix.gates_why: `review` catches it while the fix is being chosen; `reply` catches the half that is about what gets REPORTED — a temporary fix must be called temporary in the reply, which is a reply-time obligation, not a file-time one.

vendor-update-runbook.why: A moment, not a file class — it fires when an update is being taken, and the files it touches are a vendored tree whose paths differ in every consuming repo. Routed by the `merge` gate.
vendor-update-runbook.gates_why: An update lands as a merge, and the merge is the last moment the sequence can still be checked before it is someone else's committed history.

go-merge.why: A moment, and specifically a phrase in a MESSAGE -- no file path reaches it. Routed by the `merge` gate.
go-merge.decided: 2026-09-08, when it moved up from the individual set
go-merge.gates_why: Its whole subject is what happens at a merge.

park-it.why: A moment, and specifically a phrase in a MESSAGE -- no file path reaches it. Routed by the `reply` gate.
park-it.decided: 2026-09-08, when it moved up from the repo-local source
park-it.gates_why: The obligation lands in the reply: mark the item this turn, say which one, ask nothing back.

plain-words.why: A moment, and specifically a phrase in a MESSAGE -- no file path reaches it. Routed by the `reply` gate.
plain-words.decided: 2026-09-08, when the practice landed at universal
plain-words.gates_why: It governs how every reply after the phrase is written, so the reply gate is the only moment it can fire; nothing about a file triggers it.

three-things.why: A moment, and specifically a phrase in a MESSAGE -- no file path reaches it. Routed by the `reply` gate.
three-things.decided: 2026-09-08, when the practice landed at universal
three-things.gates_why: The whole obligation is the shape of one reply: three items, a bold phrase and at most two sentences each, and nothing around them.

change-updates-its-docs.why: Any change can have a reader-facing half -- a tool, a template, a config key, a practice. No glob narrower than everything describes "the thing some document describes", and a narrower one would silently exempt whichever kind of file nobody thought of.
change-updates-its-docs.gates_why: The merge is the last moment the document and the change can still land in the same commit, which is the whole rule.

no-invented-specifics.why: Every document is prose somebody could be tempted to make land with a figure that is not there. Same glob as write-like-a-human, for the same reason and the same scope.
no-invented-specifics.gates_why: The reply is where a number gets rounded up to sound better, and it is the one artifact no path glob reaches.

fixture-owns-its-state.why: Test code, in the two languages this project writes it in, plus anything under a tests/ directory or named test_* in any language. Deliberately NOT `**`: the rule is about fixtures, and routing it everywhere would fire on ordinary assignment in production code, which is the shape checkable-gets-checked warns teaches sessions to ignore a signal.
fixture-owns-its-state.gates_why: A fixture's inherited state is visible in the diff that introduces it and nowhere else afterwards -- once it is merged it reads as a passing test.

filename-separator.why: Every directory that holds files, which is every path -- the rule is about a directory's contents as a set, so no narrower glob describes it. Enforced tree-scope instead of routed.
filename-separator.gates_why: No gate: it is a property of the tree at rest, checked mechanically, not an obligation that fires at a moment.

constants-are-risk-inputs.why: No locus here. The constants it governs live in a host repo's model scripts, which this repository does not contain, and the occasion is an analysis being written rather than a file being edited. Reached through the occasion index.

slow-steps-report-and-cache.why: A property of how long something runs, not of where it lives -- a gate script, an audit and a heavy solve are all in scope and share no path. Reached through the occasion index.

_note: The gate vocabulary is closed: tools/verify_harness.py refuses an unknown gate name, and refuses a gate with no practices. Each gate names a moment with a real invocation point in this repo.
gates.review: reviewing work, or a review finding a defect
gates.reply: ending a turn and writing the reply — the stop hook
